Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:8: Now, the beginning of subduing the inclination is in the days of youth, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 961): whoever sweetens his inclination in his youth will in the end have it drawn taut over him in his old age. Why? "He who pampers his servant from youth, in the end he will become a master" (Proverbs 29:21) - the "servant" is the evil inclination, which is a servant to a person for the needs of this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:9: One must always be careful of light matters, for the evil inclination does not first trip a person up except in light matters, until from light matters he comes to grave ones, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Sukkah 52a), on the verse (Isaiah 5:18) "woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity" - their words: Rabbi Yosi said, the evil inclination is at first like a thread, and in the end like the ropes of a wagon - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:10: The author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3, reckoning 14) - his words: "Awaken, my brother, from this slumber, and cast off from your heart the veil your inclination has poured over you, until it has separated between your light and the light of your intellect - like a spider that weaves over the window of the house, and as it continues, it thickens and blocks it until it prevents the sunlight from reaching the house. At the beginning of its weaving it is very thin and weak, but the longer it continues, the stronger and thicker it becomes, until it prevents the sunlight from passing through it and reaching the house. So too the workings of the inclination in your heart: at first it will be very weak and will not prevent you from seeing the truth; and if you sense it at that time and remove it from your heart, the matter will be easy for you, but if you take it lightly and ignore it, its work will grow stronger and will prevent the light of your intellect from being able to remove it from your awareness. Therefore, hasten to save your soul, seek God's help to push it away from you, and exert effort and strive - you will be illuminated by the light of wisdom and see the truth of things with the eye of your heart. Our ancients already gave a parable for the workings of the inclination in a person, taken from the verse (II Samuel 12:4) 'and a traveler came to the rich man' - and afterward it calls him a 'wayfarer,' and afterward calls him a 'man,' and it says (Psalms 1:1) 'happy is the man who has not walked,' etc., and afterward 'stood,' and afterward 'sat'" - so far his words. Further concerning the enticements of the inclination there is a passage from the Zohar in the next chapter, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:11: Further, one must be careful and precise in his deeds regarding sins that a person treads underfoot [treats lightly], as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Mechilta (see Sifrei, Ha'azinu), and likewise in Avodah Zarah, chapter 1 (18a): Reish Lakish said, sins that a person treads underfoot in this world surround him for the Day of Judgment; and because of this the daughter of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon was punished, for Rabbi Yochanan said: once she was walking before the great men of Rome, and they said, "how lovely are the steps of this maiden!" - she immediately began to be precise about her steps [i.e., took care to walk gracefully, drawing attention], and they placed her in a brothel; and when she was brought out, she justified the judgment upon herself, [reciting] "great in counsel," etc., "whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men" (Jeremiah 32:19) - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:12: Along these lines, it is explained in the Zohar (Mikeitz 198a): Rabbi Elazar opened (Psalms 49:6) "why should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels surrounds me?" Come and see: there are three kinds who fear yet do not know what they fear, as has been established; but there is one who fears yet does not know what he fears - such as those sins he does not know are sins and does not pay attention to - and he fears "the days of evil." What are "the days of evil"? These are days appointed for that evil. And what is "that evil"? This is the evil inclination, which is called "evil," and it has known days when permission is given to it in the world to lead astray all those whose ways are defiled - for whoever comes to defile himself, they defile him - and these are called "days of evil," and they are appointed over those sins that people tread underfoot with their heels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:13: Come and see: all those whose ways are defiled - how many bundles of impure spirits gather to them and defile them; on the very path a person wishes to walk, they lead him astray in fact, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:14: Come and see: at the time when harsh judgment rules, it does not withhold its hand from doing harm; but at the time when the right rules over the idolatrous nations to break them, the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on them and does not destroy them; and therefore, whoever sins in those sins he treads underfoot without knowing them should always fear them. David the king was always careful to guard against these sins, and when he went out to war he would examine himself for them, and therefore he did not fear to wage war against them. And come and see: four kings [in the war of the kings, Genesis 14] - what one [angel] asked, the other did not ask, etc. Therefore a person must guard himself from these sins, as it says, so that those "days of evil" not rule over him, days that show no mercy toward him - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:15: Concerning something similar, the Torah commanded that the priest anointed for war would speak to the people and say (Deuteronomy 20:8) "who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted," and it is explained (Sotah, chapter 8, mishnah 5) that this refers to one who fears the transgressions in his hand; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 36a) that one who speaks [an interruption] between the hand-tefillin and the head-tefillin must return to the ranks [i.e., is disqualified] from those who array for war [an allusion applied there].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:16: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Bava Kama, chapter "An Ox that Gored a Cow" (50a): whoever says the Holy One, blessed be He, is lenient [foregoes strict justice] - his life will be forfeited [lit., "foregone"], as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4) "the Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice" - so far. And they said further there - their words: (Psalms 50:3) "and it is very tempestuous round about Him" - this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with His pious ones even to a hair's breadth. Rabbi Chanina said, this is derived from here (Psalms 89:8) "God is dreaded in the great council of holy ones, and feared above all who surround Him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:17: Further, they said in Bereishit Rabbah (19:1): "for in much wisdom is much vexation, and he who increases knowledge increases pain" (Ecclesiastes 1:18) - from here we learn that the more wisdom a person acquires, the more vexation increases upon him, and the more knowledge he adds, the more pain is added, etc. Rav said, a scholar [chaver] does not need forewarning [before being liable]; Rabbi Yochanan said, it is like fine linen garments that come from Beit She'an - if they get slightly scorched, they are ruined, but coarse linen garments - how much are they, and how much are they worth [i.e., minor damage doesn't matter]? It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: according to the greatness of the serpent was its downfall - it was more cunning than all and more cursed than all - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:18: Further, one must fear and be careful in his deeds, for perhaps he himself and the world are half meritorious and half guilty, and he tips the scale for himself and for the whole world to the side of guilt. So too our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 40b): our Rabbis taught, a person should always regard himself as though he were half meritorious and half guilty; if he performs one mitzvah, happy is he, for he has tipped the scale for himself to the side of merit; if he commits one transgression, woe to him, for he has tipped the scale for himself to the side of guilt, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:18) "and one sinner destroys much good" - because of the single sin he committed, this person loses much good. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: since the world is judged according to its majority, and the individual is judged according to his majority - if he performs one mitzvah, happy is he, for he has tipped the scale for himself and for the whole world to the side of merit; if he commits one transgression, woe to him, for he has tipped the scale for himself and for the whole world to the side of guilt, as it is said, "and one sinner destroys much good" - because of the single sin he committed, this person loses, for himself and for the world, much good - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:19: Of this kind of fear is the fear of the judgment that resides in the Shechinah, as it says in the Idra (Ha'azinu 292a), in the words of Rabbi Shimon: "all my days I have been troubled that the world not be burned by His judgments of righteousness." One must fear lest he be the cause of the world being burned in judgments, for perhaps the world is half meritorious and half guilty, and if, God forbid, he tips the whole world to the side of guilt and causes, through him, pestilence or famine to come upon the world - all those righteous ones who died, he is the cause of their death, and all the poor who cry out and die of hunger, he is the cause for them - and this is "woe to him," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:20: Therefore one must always take care never to be idle from Torah or a mitzvah, as they said in the Talmud (Menachot 41a): an angel found Rav Katina wrapped in a sheet [without tzitzit as required, in a garment exempt by its material]... he said to him, do you punish for [the omission of] a positive commandment? He said to him, at a time when there is wrath [in the world], we do punish. We find, then, that they punish for the neglect of a mitzvah at a time when there is anger in the world; and engaging in Torah is a positive commandment, and there is no doubt that they punish for its neglect as well - it was not necessary to mention it, since Rabbi Katina was not idle from Torah. Therefore one must be exceedingly careful and diligent in his labor, the labor of Heaven, so as not to be found idle and thereby be punished - for at a time of wrath, the attribute of righteous judgment rules in its judgments, and one must be careful lest the world be burned by its judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:21: At all times a person is obligated to supply the oil of Torah and mitzvot to the lamp upon his head, "for the Lord your God is a consuming fire," as is explained in the portion of Bereishit (Zohar 51a-b); how much more so, God forbid, at a time of wrath, when great care and diligence are required, since it is within his power to correct matters and draw down an abundance of mercy, to turn the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy - and one who is lazy will be punished, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:22: We find that Rabbah, peace be upon him, called himself "average." They said in Berachot (61b): Rabbah said, one such as I is average. Abaye said to him, our master leaves no life for any creature [i.e., if you consider yourself only average, who would be righteous]. And Rabbah said, a person knows within himself whether he is completely righteous or completely wicked. And Rabbah said, the world was created only for the completely righteous or the completely wicked. And Rabbah said, the whole world was created only for the sake of Ahab son of Omri and for the sake of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa - for Ahab, this world; for Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, the World to Come - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:23: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah (4:2), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 6:7) "all the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the soul is not satisfied" - their words: "'and yet the soul is not satisfied' - because this soul knows that whatever it toils, it toils for itself, and therefore it is never satisfied with mitzvot and good deeds. Rabbi Levi said: [it is like] a commoner married to a princess - even if he feeds her all the delicacies of the world, he has not fulfilled his obligation to her, because she is a princess. So too, whatever a person does for the soul, he has not fulfilled his obligation to it, because it is from above" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:24: Further, several things that arouse a person to be precise in his deeds and to be careful of sin are explained in Tractate Chagigah (4b) - their words: "Rabbi Ami, when he reached this verse, wept (Lamentations 3:29) 'let him put his mouth in the dust, perhaps there is hope' - he said, all this, and only 'perhaps'! Rabbi Ami, when he reached this verse, wept (Zephaniah 2:3) 'seek righteousness, seek humility, perhaps you shall be hidden on the day of the Lord's anger' - he said, all this, and only 'perhaps'! Rabbi Assi, when he reached this verse, wept (Amos 5:15) 'hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps the Lord, God of hosts, will be gracious' - he said, all this, and only 'perhaps'! Rav Yosef, when he reached this verse, wept (Proverbs 13:23) 'and there is one swept away without justice' - he said, is there a person who departs [the world] before his time? Yes, such as this... Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Job 2:3) 'and you incited Me against him, to destroy him without cause' - a servant whose master is incited against him has no remedy. Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (ibid. 15:15) 'behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones' - in whom, then, will He put trust?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:25: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Malachi 3:5) "and I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers and against the adulterers and against those who swear falsely and against those who oppress the hired worker in his wages" - a servant against whom his master draws near to judge him and is swift to testify against him has no remedy. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said: woe to us, for Scripture equates light [sins] with grave ones - light with grave: Rashi explains, [it equates] those who oppress the hired worker's wages with adulterers and sorcerers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:26: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Ecclesiastes 12:14) "for God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing" - a servant whose master weighs his unintentional acts as though they were deliberate has no remedy. What is meant by "including every hidden thing"? Rav said, this refers to one who kills a louse in front of his fellow and is repulsed by it [i.e., considers even that trivial act a matter for judgment]; and Shmuel said, this refers to one who spits in front of his fellow and is repulsed by it. What is meant by "whether it is good or evil"? Rashi explains, that even for a good deed He brings a person into judgment. It was said in the school of Rabbi Yannai, this refers to one who gives charity to a poor person publicly, as with Rabbi Yannai, who saw a certain man giving a coin to a poor man in public; he said to him, "better that you had not given it to him at all than that you gave it to him now and shamed him." It was said in the school of Rabbi Yannai, this refers to one who gives charity to a woman in private, which brings her under suspicion. Rava said, this refers to one who sends meat to his wife that is not [fully] cut up - Rashi explains, that has not been checked for forbidden fat and sinews on Friday afternoons [before Shabbat], since due to their haste to prepare for Shabbat, they do not pay attention to whether it has been checked. But did Rava himself send such meat? - his wife, the daughter of Rav Chisda, was different, since he was confident in her [that she would check it properly].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:27: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Deuteronomy 31:21) "and it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles have come upon him" - a servant for whom his master brings about evils and troubles has no remedy. And they said further there: Rabbi Ila was ascending the staircase of the house of Rabbah bar Shela; he heard a child reciting (Amos 4:13) "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his speech [sicho]" - he said, a servant to whom his master declares his own speech has no remedy. What is "his speech"? Rav said, even idle conversation between a man and his wife is declared to a person at the time of death - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:1: One must fear sin, for in several ways the sinner angers the Creator, blessed be He. The first is what Scripture says (Jeremiah 23:24) "if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the Lord; do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord." This verse is explained in Midrash Tanchuma (Naso 4-5): "'if a man hides himself in secret places,' etc. - a parable of an architect who built a city and made secret tunnels within it, etc. So too the Holy One, blessed be He, says to adulterers: from Me you hide yourselves? As it is said (Job 24:15) 'and the eye of the adulterer watches for the twilight, saying, no eye shall see me, and he puts a covering over his face' - the adulterer says, no creature knows of me, and my eyes rove over the whole earth. What is the way of those who commit transgressions? They watch for the hour of darkness, the hour of night - and so too the thieves - 'in the dark he digs through houses' (Job, ibid. 16); and so it says (Isaiah 29:15) 'woe to those who dig deep to hide their counsel from the Lord, and their deeds are in the dark, and they say, who sees us and who knows us?' The adulterer is worse, for he, as it were, removes the Shechinah - He who fills the upper and lower worlds, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:24) 'do I not fill the heaven and the earth?' - and in what place is this man committing adultery? When he comes to commit adultery, he says to the Omnipresent, remove Yourself and give me one moment; and, as it were, because He is slow to anger, He gives him room, as it is said (Job 11:11) 'for He knows men of falsehood, and sees iniquity, will He not then consider it?' and it says 'and puts a covering over his face' - [they ask that she not conceive from him, but only that their desire be fulfilled, not knowing that the Holy One, blessed be He, publicizes them to the world] - He who sits in the supernal secret place puts a face upon [the child] so that it is recognized she conceived from him; the child's form is fashioned and its face resembles the adulterer" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:2: It is explained that there are two kinds of ugliness and disgrace in the sinner: the first, that he demeans the King by saying that He does not watch over him when he hides himself - this is "if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the Lord" - and here the sense pauses. "Do I not fill the heaven and the earth?" is the second blemish, that he, as it were, removes the Shechinah - the Holy One, blessed be He, fills [everything], etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:3: Along these lines, they said in the Mishnah (Chagigah, chapter 2, mishnah 1): whoever does not care for the honor of his Maker, it would have been better for him not to have come into the world. They said in the Talmud (Chagigah 16a): Rav Yosef said, this refers to one who transgresses in secret, for Rabbi Yitzchak said, whoever transgresses in secret is as though he pushes against the feet of the Shechinah, as it is said (Isaiah 66:1) "the heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:4: Along these lines, they said in Berachot, chapter "The Morning Prayer" (28b): when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his disciples came to visit him... they said to him, our teacher, bless us. He said to them, "may it be [God's] will that the fear of Heaven be upon you as the fear of flesh and blood." They said to him, our teacher, [is that] as far as it goes [i.e., no higher]? He said to them, "would that it be so! Know that when a person transgresses in secret, he says, let no one see me" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:5: Along these lines is the parable stated in the midrash concerning "if a man hides himself in secret places," etc. Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Noach 68a): "Rabbi Chiya opened (Jeremiah 23:24) 'if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the Lord.' How many people are there whose hearts are sealed and whose eyes are closed, who do not pay heed and do not know the glory of their Master, of whom it is written 'do I not fill the heaven and the earth?' How do they wish to hide from their sins and say, 'who sees us and who knows us?' - yet it is written 'and their deeds are in the dark.' Where will they hide from before Him? [It is like] a king who built a palace and made hidden crevices beneath the ground; in time, the members of the king's palace rebelled, and the king brought his troops upon them in distress. What did they do? They went and hid themselves in those hidden crevices. The king said, I am the one who made them, and I made light and darkness, and from before me you wish to hide? This is [the meaning of] 'if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the Lord' - I am He who made the hidden crevices and made darkness and light, and how can you hide from before Me? Come and see: when a person sins before his Master and draws himself to be concealed, the Holy One, blessed be He, executes judgment upon him openly; but when a person purifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to conceal him so that he not be seen on the day of the Lord's wrath" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:6: In Midrash Bemidbar Rabbah, portion 9 (paragraph 1), a similar parable is brought concerning the adulterer and the adulteress, and they say in the moral of the parable - their words: "So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to adulterers: from Me you hide yourselves, yet is it not I who created hearts? As it is said (Jeremiah 17:10) 'I, the Lord, search the heart and test the kidneys,' etc.; therefore it is said 'and you forgot God who formed you [mecholelecha]' - I created you and made you full of hollows [mechilim] - these are the hearts and kidneys - and you forget Me and are false to Me: 'I do not see and I do not know your deeds'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:7: Concerning the particulars of Divine providence, Elihu said (Job 34:21-22) "for His eyes are upon the ways of a man, and He sees all his steps; there is no darkness nor deep shadow where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:8: Further, he angers Him in a second way, in that His attribute, blessed be He, is to do good and show mercy, and they turn it from the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereishit Rabbah 33:3): cursed are the wicked, who turn the attribute of mercy into the attribute of judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:9: What is written (Psalms 145:9) "and His mercies are upon all His works" - our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Tanchuma (Yalkut Nachum, remez 561) that this refers to the righteous - their words, on the verse (Nachum 1:7) "the Lord is good, a stronghold" - one might think for everyone; the text teaches, "and He knows those who take refuge in Him" - only for them. Similarly (Lamentations 3:25) "the Lord is good to those who hope for Him" - one might think for everyone; the text teaches, "to the soul that seeks Him" - only for such a one. Similarly (Psalms 145:9) "the Lord is good to all" - one might think for everyone; the text teaches, "and His mercies are upon all His works" - so far, as relevant to us. And "His works" [ma'asav] refers to the righteous, since they are the works particularly His, along the lines of (Isaiah 60:21) "and your people, all of them righteous,... the work of My hands, in which I glory." So too in the Zohar, portion of Lech Lecha (82b), the righteous are the fruit of the works of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:10: Further, they said in the Tanchuma (Bechukotai 2), on the verse (Hosea 9:17) "my God will reject them because they have not listened to Him, and they shall be wanderers among the nations," etc.: the Holy One, blessed be He, said, I am called "the Lord, God, merciful and gracious," but because of your sins He makes Himself cruel, as it is said (Lamentations 2:5) "the Lord has become like an enemy" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:11: Of this kind is the matter that whoever commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser (Avot 4:11), and the accuser stands to accuse and to arouse the powers of judgment, until a portion of judgment is given to him to exact payment from the one who committed it; and this is (Job 34:11) "for according to the deed of a man He repays him," as is explained in the Zohar, portion of Korach (177a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:12: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 145b): "your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates, they have become a burden to Me" (Isaiah 1:14) - what is the meaning of "they have become a burden to Me"? Rabbi Elazar said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: it is not enough for the wicked that they sin, but they also burden Me with having to decide which harsh decree to bring upon them - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:13: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Tanchuma, on the verse (Jeremiah 3:19) "and I said, how shall I place you among the children [eshitcha]?" - Rabbi Elazar ben Padat said: what is meant by "eshitcha"? It arose in My thought that I and you would be alone in the world; how could you do this to Me, to bring in the nations of the world among you? And this expression means only "separation," as it says (Genesis 30:40) "and he set [vayashet] separate flocks for himself." Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: there was great love between Me and you; how could you do this to Me, that I should hate you? And this expression means only "hatred," as it is said (Genesis 3:15) "and I will put [ashit] enmity." Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: I speak in your defense; how could you do this to Me, that I should accuse you and find you guilty? And this expression means only "guilt," as it is said (Exodus 21:30) "if a ransom is laid [yushat] upon him." Rabbi Berachyah said: you were as dear to Me as a man who has one field, which he fertilizes and hoes and weeds; how could you do this to Me, to make yourselves ownerless? And this expression means only "ownerless," as it is said (Isaiah 5:6) "and I will make it [ashitehu] a wasteland" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:14: Four aspects of love that the Holy One, blessed be He, has for Israel are explained in this passage, and because of our sins they were all turned to hatred; and it is possible to ascribe them to the four letters of the Name in their order, and each Tanna who mentioned one of these aspects does not disagree with the others - the discerning reader will understand the matter for himself. And I will hint to you a little: Rabbi Berachyah said the last of these, corresponding to the final Heh: "you were as dear to Me as a man who has one field," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:15: Further, a third [aspect]: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry at the wicked, and all Israel is punished on his account. So too in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah (4:6) - their words: "'Israel is a scattered sheep' (Jeremiah 50:17) - Israel is compared to a sheep: just as it is the way of a sheep that if it is struck in one of its limbs, they all feel it, so too if one Israelite sins, all are punished. Rashbi taught: this is like two men who were in a boat, and one of them took a drill and began drilling beneath his own seat. His companions said to him, why are you doing this? He said to them, what does it matter to you? I am only drilling under my own place. They said to him, because you are flooding the boat upon us! So too Job said (Job 19:4) 'and even if I have truly erred, my error remains with me' - his companions said to him (ibid. 34:37) 'for he adds rebellion to his sin, he claps [his hands mockingly] among us' - you are adding our sins upon us" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:16: Further, a fourth [aspect]: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry at the wicked because He gave him a good way and an evil way, and he abandoned the good. So too they said in Midrash Tehillim, on the verse (Psalms 36:5) "he plans iniquity on his bed, he sets himself on a way that is not good" - their words: He gave them two ways, one evil and one good, and they abandon the good and go in the evil, as it says (Proverbs 2:13) "who leave the paths of uprightness," etc., "who rejoice to do evil," etc. - hence, "he sets himself on a way that is not good" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:17: Further, a fifth: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry at the wicked because of the evil he causes to himself and to his own soul on account of his sin. Our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Tehillim, on the verse (Psalms 51:9) "purify me with hyssop and I shall be clean" - their words: from here [we learn] that whoever commits a transgression is as though he became defiled by contact with a dead body, and one is sprinkled clean only with hyssop, as it is said "purify me with hyssop and I shall be clean." But was David defiled? Rather, it is the sin that has made his soul a corpse [chalal - pierced/slain], as it is also said (ibid. 109:22) "and my heart is slain [chalal] within me" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:18: To understand this matter properly - how a person blemishes his own soul such that we can say he has killed it and made it a corpse - we must know what is agreed upon in the Zohar (Mishpatim 94b) and in the Tikkunim (79a): that a person has ruach, nefesh, and neshamah, and there is [also] nefesh, ruach, and neshamah in the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (79a), and likewise at the beginning of the portion of Mishpatim (94b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:19: One must know that just as the physical person has two hundred and forty-eight physical limbs, so the soul that is clothed within these two hundred and forty-eight limbs has two hundred and forty-eight spiritual limbs, and the soul is what is truly called "Adam," as I explained above; for what is said (Genesis 1:27) "and God created man [Adam] in His image" refers to the soul, since the body is called "the flesh of man," as it is said (Exodus 30:32) "upon the flesh of man it shall not be poured." So too Rashbi explains (Bereishit 20b) - his words: "the spirit, on the holy side, [whose] body is [given] a garment - it is Adam, and therefore it is written (Job 10:11) 'You have clothed me with skin and flesh,' etc. - the flesh of Adam is their garment, and everywhere it is written 'the flesh of man' - Adam is within, flesh is the garment of Adam" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:20: Because the soul is comprised of two hundred and forty-eight spiritual limbs, it acts and clothes itself in that drop [of semen] to fashion a vessel for its work, and thus the body is the mold of the soul; and for this reason people's forms differ by the thousands and the tens of thousands according to the quarry of their souls, as is explained in the Tikkunim (128a-b).
